newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala made no deal to free envoy - official.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala made no deal to free envoy - official.

text.p: Marxist guerrillas holding more than 100 VIP hostages in Peru made an independent decision to free the Guatemalan ambassador on Thursday, Foreign Minister Eduardo Stein said.
"His freedom was not conditional in any way," Stein told reporters. There was no negotiation between Guatemala and the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Army (MRTA), he added.

Stein said Guatemalan Ambassador Jose Maria Argueta had held long conversations with the rebels before being freed from the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima. The MRTA has held hostages there for more than a week.

"The MRTA told him that they freed him as a show of recognition of Guatemalans' efforts for internal reconciliation. They support our peace efforts," said Stein, who spoke with Argueta by telephone after he was freed.
The Guatemalan government and leftist rebels of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) will sign a peace treaty on Sunday ending 36 years of civil war.
The treaty follows five years of often-rocky negotiations between the government and the rebels.

Unlike Central American nations with guerrillas, all of which ended years of violence through negotiation, Peru under President Alberto Fujimori has followed a strong-arm approach to breaking up such movements.
Fujimori continued his tough position by refusing to negotiate during the hostage crisis.
"We maintain a respectful but firm stance that Guatemala endorses negotiation efforts for a peaceful end to the crisis, and we hope that good judgment will prevail," Stein said.
He said Argueta was in "perfect health" despite having to sleep on the floor and would return to Guatemala on Saturday.
